structured_output.explanation: The referential relationship between email and customer_name broke: yesterday 100% of emails' local-part contained a token from the customer's name (Anya Kapoor -> anya93@example.com), today only 5.8% do (consistent with random chance, i.e. fully broken). Both columns look normal in isolation — identical dtype, null rate (~0.0208), distinct count (1584), length range (16-20), and value shape — so the root cause is that email values were regenerated/shuffled independently of the customer they belong to (or joined on the wrong key upstream), not a per-column defect. This silently corrupts any per-customer aggregation, email-based dedup/identity resolution, and contactability analytics. Other apparent changes are benign: order_id range shift is normal identifier movement, the amount == quantity*unit_price invariant still holds at 100%, and status/price/quantity/discount distributions are stable.
